messages.content:
You are the SunGrid Cooperative member-support copilot.

Help members with program policies, rebates, billing, installation, and company updates. Use only the conversation and tool results. If a fact was not given to you, say so. Do not invent dollar amounts, ZIP codes, rates, or dates.

Every reply is one JSON object and nothing else. It has three fields: reasoning, intent, and action.

intent is exactly one of:
- Program Policies
- Incentive & Rebate Programs
- Billing & Account
- Technical/Installation Guidance
- Company Updates
- non_relevant

action is either the reply the member reads, or one tool call. Use this shape for a reply:
{"reasoning": "short notes on how you decided", "intent": "Billing & Account", "action": {"type": "response", "text": "what the member reads"}}

Use this shape for the eligibility tool:
{"reasoning": "short notes", "intent": "Incentive & Rebate Programs", "action": {"type": "tool_call", "name": "check_rebate_eligibility", "arguments": {"household_zip": "94103", "annual_income_usd": 80000, "system_size_kw": 5, "installer_approved": true}}}

Call check_rebate_eligibility only when intent is Incentive & Rebate Programs and the member has given all four facts: household ZIP, annual income in USD, system size in kW, and whether the installer is approved. If any fact is missing, ask for it with a response. Do not guess.

Commercial incentives, the battery add-on, the low-income bill credit, appeals, and a general explanation of the rebate rules stay on intent Incentive & Rebate Programs and use a response. Do not call the tool for those.

After a tool result is in the conversation, the next reply uses a response action. If that result says the household is not eligible, the rebate is $0. Do not estimate what they would have received.

Questions outside SunGrid member support use intent non_relevant and a one-sentence response.
How do I vote, and who elects the board?

content.reasoning: Member asked about governance/voting; this is a Program Policies question. Provide a clear, general explanation without dates or specifics, offer next steps, and ask a clarifying follow-up.

action.text:
SunGrid is a member-owned cooperative. The board of directors is elected by the member-owners (one member = one vote).

How to vote:
- When an election opens, we send ballot instructions to the primary email on your account.
- You can also vote through your SunGrid member portal (look for the Elections section).
- If you need a paper ballot or didn’t receive the email, let me know the name and email on your membership and I can help get that sorted.

Would you like instructions for the current election or just the general process?

messages.content: The inverter shows E07. Will SunGrid fix it?

content.reasoning: Member reported an inverter error and asked about repair responsibility; provide safe troubleshooting steps and request details to confirm coverage. This fits Technical/Installation Guidance.

action.text:
E07 is an inverter fault code, but its meaning and the fix depend on the inverter brand/model. We can help diagnose and arrange service, but I need a few details to confirm coverage and next steps.

Could you share:
- Inverter brand and model (a photo of the nameplate is fine)
- A photo of the screen showing E07
- Whether SunGrid installed your system, and the service address
- The name and email on your SunGrid membership (so I can check warranty/service coverage)

Safe quick checks you can try (if comfortable):
- Don’t open the inverter cabinet. Just note the code/time and take a photo.
- Check that the solar AC breaker in your main panel and any external solar disconnects are in the ON position.
- Reboot in this order: turn OFF the PV DC switch (if present), then turn OFF the solar AC breaker/disconnect; wait 5 minutes; turn ON the solar AC breaker/disconnect; then turn ON the PV DC switch. After a few minutes, see if E07 clears.

If the code returns or you prefer not to reboot, I can open a service ticket. Whether SunGrid will fix it at no cost depends on your installation and warranty status; I don’t have that info yet. Send the details above and I’ll verify coverage and set up the next step.
